top_comments.author: Rosie_The_ITTech
top_comments.body:
Mainly two things :

First, the fact that racing is the worst possible way of getting away from rookie. I've made more progress in one afternoon of starting from the pit lane, regardless of my qualifying position, staying as far away from the pack as possible than I had in weeks of racing in the pack, trying to keep it clean but always ending up collected by a dive bomber charging from my blind spot for a passing lane that never existed.

Second, people who will explain to you that you're entirely at fault for daring to exist in front of a dive bomber at an entry corner and that you should always let them pass you, but who then will also criticize anybody who voluntarily stay away from the pack because "you're not learning defensive driving if you just avoid other driver".

  
If I want to do a Demolition Derby I can just play Wreckfest, it's cheaper, less frustrating, and the driving is actually much MUCH better than open wheeler rookie class here. I see no difference between purposefully avoiding the good cornering line to deal with dive bomber and giving them a 15 second head start altogether. In  both case I'm screwing up my lap so they can do whatever they want and I don't have to bear the consequences or their bs. (Because yeah, if dive bombers cared about their SR ratting, they wouldn't dive bomb)

1n0hnpo.title: I'm so tired of these weeks... economic system makes me want to quit the game

top_comments.author: Slowleytakenusername
top_comments.body:
You could be doing daily races at Interlagos and Monza this week and you could join a race at Imola or Fuji in the online championship. Already pointed out how the base game has 7 tracks and that they limit the content in the beginner series to content that is in the base game. That is no different to how iRacing handels the rookie series. If you only join beginner races than you will more likely see the same tracks on rotation. 

Let's be a bit more fair in the comparisson to iRacing. iRacing has existed since 2008 and has putting putting out content for a long time. Yeah your going to have more content but LMU is in the proces of adding more content and at a lower price compared to iRacing. Silverstone, Paul Ricard and Barcelona are also coming to LMU.

top_comments.author: TonAmiChris
top_comments.body: I feel like the “for me” is implied already? What’s the point of this comment?

top_comments.author: Slowleytakenusername
top_comments.body:
Yeah, I have now learned that this is just the nature of lower split racing. I was fed up with ACC LFM racing because of the wild crap I was seeing on some tracks (T1 on the Nurburgring was always a pile up). People warned me that it was going to be the same in iRacing but I went anyway and started liking it for other reasons. But they were right, it was a ramfest at the lower splits. LMU is not different and I'm sure it is the same for others sims. 

What I have learned is to just deal with it and work on pace. Once you get faster you can just drive away from the chaos and move up to better splits.

top_comments.author: Slowleytakenusername
top_comments.body:
What he he wrote is a 100% true if you actually red what he wrote. If you wanted to run a full season of GT3 or IMSA, you have had to have bought content every season. 2 reasons for that. 

One is that they always ad the new track into the season. Many of the road series added the Bend so even if you had spent a 1000 bucks in the season before that, you had to buy that track to run a full season in GT4, GT3, IMSA and the Production Car Challenge. 

Second is that they always manage to ad 2 tracks that have not been in the series for the past 4 seasons. That way, every player that has not been on the service for longer than a year is going to have to buy a minimum of 3 tracks every season to race all races in their prefered season. I started iRacing march 2024 and I was buying 4 tracks every season up untill last season to compete in every race of the GT3 fixed and sprint series. Past season was the only season I did not buy a track because I was on a holiday on those weeks the tracks ran and LMU made me lose interest in iRacing. 

Yeah you're not forced to buy anything and you could run a different series but I don't think that is a good argument for a person that wants to run a certain series.

top_comments.author: Slowleytakenusername
top_comments.body:
You're either shitposting of being extremely dishonst. The Base game comes with 7 tracks, 9 hypercars, 1 LMP2, 4 GTE cars and 2 GT3 cars. You can get an additional 11 cars and 4 tracks by buying all the DLC for about $70 (converted the price from €, price may be even lower for US players). It also has new DLC coming that will ad new tracks and cars. 11 cars and 4 tracks in iRacing would cost you $150 if you get the 20% discount (most won't get that when starting).

The way LMU is structured is that in the Daily beginner races the tracks are always something that is in the base game. For intermediate and advanced atleast one of the 2 races is a track from the base content. You can compete at any level without ever having to buy a single piece of DLC. Lets compare that to iRacing and trying to do a season of GT3 or IMSA. 10 out of 12 tracks in that series you have to buy. That is 10x$14,99 and one car at $11,99. And you just know that any new track that comes out new is going to be forced into the next season of any popular series. You either buy it or you sit out one week of the series you enjoy doing.

We all agree that iRacing has more content but you're paying a very high price to enjoy that content. Also keep in mind that iRacing has been around for forever while LMU only released in 2024. But it's not just about the content, the quality is IMO more important. If it is just about quantity and we go by your logic, than Gran Turimo 7 blows iRacing (and LMU)out of the water. It has 38 locations with 118 variants and 526 cars all in the base game. And you can get that game for 30 bucks on sale.

I understand very well that you are not forced to buy anything in iRacing and you can hang out in rookies forever and just pay the subscription fee. But most people want to do a certain serieus and if for example, you enjoy doing GT3's than you're going to pay alot. They even make it hard for you to progress through the SR ratings without buying content. I gave up on getting my A license for Ovals because I was forced to do C level races and there were only a minimal amount of base content tracks in those series meaning I had to wait for weeks to give it another shot or pay the iRacing premium. Annoying part is that they ad road courses in the oval series that don't count to you oval license SR. Ad all that to there not being many people in my time zone doing ovals and it becomes very frustrating.

**TL;DR:** The base content in LMU lets you race any class at any level and all the extra content in the game costs a fraction of the cost of doing one GT3/IMSA season in iRacing.

1q4nm3y.title: Sim Racing burnout - should I wait any longer?

top_comments.author: kaozer
top_comments.body: Ive been taking a break myself after the driving standards on iracing made me question why im doing all this. It was a year or so ago, but now the itch is coming back. Id say dont force it. At some point the track will call for you!

top_comments.author: Dull-Ad-6147
top_comments.body:
I think this hobby, like all others, is something you either love or hate, it's that simple. I've been a sim racer since I was 17. I started with a €20 steering wheel and my mom's armchair. Now I'm 48 and I have a really good, complete setup with a triple monitor that I've had for at least 10 years. I'm always improving/upgrading it, but what gives me the most pleasure is racing, more than improving the setup. That's why I love it, obviously. And I'm not some mega-star just because I've been doing it for almost 30 years. I have a 2.5k iR in iRacing and I enjoy every race immensely. I also do rallies. One of these days I'll get into flight simulators; they've always intrigued me, but I'd need two sim rigs and that's not going to happen, so I'll stick with sim racing. If I ever get tired of it, I'll switch to flying, maybe when I'm 60, haha.
Wow, that was a long post. What I wanted to say is that if running doesn't motivate you, don't run and sell, that's it. Cheers.

top_comments.author: Firm-Painting5257
top_comments.body: I get burnout from racing or flying all the time. I just move onto something else. It's alot easier to do with friends though, I will say that!

top_comments.author: Feeling_Piglet215
top_comments.body: You're missing a goal every time you go racing/playing… Can I get 0.4 seconds off my lap time on this track or sector? How do I do it? Do I stiffen a sway bar? Lower the traction control? Increase the ABS?… I come from Xbox, where I used to play ACC with great friends I met online. I had a blast racing with them while we chatted! Now that I'm on PC, my group of friends is too small, not to mention lonely, and I miss that. But my motivation is to try to improve and compete with the best. It's very satisfying when, at the end of each race, you and another driver congratulate each other in the iRacing general chat; it lets you know you're doing things right. Obviously, there will be races where you want to sell everything and never play again, but when you start racing intelligently, you enjoy it so much more! Keep it up, mate!

top_comments.body: do not sell ! i promise that itch comes back hard. keep the rig and disappear into elite dangerous or star citizen.

1qhe53w.title: Genuine question. What makes wheels like this... so expensive?

top_comments.author: n19htmare
top_comments.body:
Every industry has their subset of "audiophiles", 75 year olds with degenerative hearing loss who swear by their half dug graves that they hear the tone of a cymbal better on their $80,000 speakers powered by $40,000 amp than something that costs a fraction.

Likely not many 75 year olds in this hobby but the point is these companies are targeting a niche with-in a niche, around the world, and they've decided there are enough of these people to make it worthwhile. Fact that it has a Simucube license already means it's not targeting people with Simagic, Moza users.

Is it "worth it"? To vast majority of us, no, it's not. But there's enough people to whom it might be.

top_comments.author: JamesConsonants
top_comments.body:
> The feel and refinement

That premium "feel" comes from tighter manufacturing tolerances and high-quality tactile encoders, buttons and switches. As you decrease your machining tolerances, you exponentially increase the cost to manufacture, either in the form of more expensive outsourcing or increasing the time it takes to manufacture a unit in-house. 

For reference, I am currently building a wheel rim loosely based on the Merc F1 wheel to have enough I/O to control the VRC FA2024 via simhub: (9 rotary encoders, 13 momentary switches, 21LEDs, an arduino, LCD screen, USB connectors, cables/wiring, quick release) etc. and the bill of materials for that project was around $150 for mid-grade hardware. If I used the encoders that I originally wanted to use, all other things being equal, that bill would be close to double. 

As with anything, it's a balance between cost and quality. If you want encoders/switches that won't accidentally change position when bumped, you have to pay for it. That's the market that these premium products aim to service, not your average AC Hotlap Enjoyer.

top_comments.author: Wooden-Agent2669
top_comments.body: Because a Wheel is not going to improve your lap times by a second or more.

top_comments.author: n19htmare
top_comments.body:
$7 retail maybe, not in bulk/wholesale. Same way Fanatec buttons might be cheaper but they're even more cheaper in large volumes and Fanatec produces a much larger volume than Ascher.

There can still be very high quality wheels for less, like some of Conspit wheels for example. I've used both, would I pay 3x as much for an Ascher? No probably not. Yes they are nicer but not 3x nicer. Their cost is high because they're low volume AND they need to pull out western salaries out of those wheels. Which is fine to support, nothing against that but to say high quality "premium" wheels can' tbe done for less, sure they can. Just not out of US/EU/Canada, that's all.

1vjzggm.title: The Frustrating Reality of Being a Mid-Pack Top Split Driver

top_comments.author: Klopapier210
top_comments.body: No there are not. But this is a game for sim racers. 99.9% of us are amateurs not making any money. Would be nice to get the chance without needing to be in the Top 100 LMU Players (Many of them actually making money from it)

top_comments.author: Klopapier210
top_comments.body:
Just to make one thing clear: I don't wanna fight for a podium each race! I want it to be something special. I'm just complaining about the reality, that I might the chance of a podium every 50 races maybe.

I also don't really like those Pro comparisons. I'm an amateur. It's not my job and I don't make money with it. I just want to have the chance to fight for a big result once in a while.

top_comments.author: Sharkbait1737
top_comments.body:
At some point if you’re half way decent you have to recognise that you’re not the fastest driver, probably never will be and either come to terms with and enjoy making incremental improvements, know enough to know you did the best race you could, and the enjoyment of driving itself.

If you are in sim racing for pure results you’re going to find it very unsatisfying once you hit those intermediate stages.

But that doesn’t mean it’s an unfulfilling hobby. I’m not all that good at woodworking or solving Rubik’s cubes or playing chess, but there is simple pleasure in learning new skills and improving at them.

Would you say a win in a crap split when you were off your pace and span the car is more satisfying to you than running consistently at your maximum and finishing 10th in top split? Because objectively the latter should be more gratifying.

top_comments.author: HumanWay8280
top_comments.body: Learned skill makes up a certain percentage of how good you are at something. As your age your potential skill ceiling is lowered. At a certain point your age will restrict you on how good you can get at something that requires physical effort and coordination

Im in a similar position in IRacing and I have basically stopped doing official races........ I'm mainly doing AI racing which I love because I can set it up to maximize my enjoyment/convenience but eventually Im gonna join some leagues too. Similarly I do track days IRL and while I'm quick in my group I'm never the fastest rider. Often some actual racers come in for practice and blow my fairings off. I have so many other things to focus on/enjoy besides getting the fastest lap in my group (they give us transponders)

So yea on one hand I get it but on the other hand this is a result of the approach you chose
